competitors.label: lazy
competitors.selectionReason: The React reference for lazy is the canonical source for component-level code splitting rules.
theirStrengths: Authoritative rules: default export only, the cached promise, rejection to the nearest error boundary, and top-level declaration.
theirGaps: API-centric: no guidance on where to split, no deploy failures and no module federation.

realWorldUseCases: It contains the storefront every visitor needs, plus an admin dashboard, a charting library and a rich-text editor that only a few users ever open
The reference explains lazy loading with a Markdown preview toggle, an API example rather than a production splitting plan.
actionableExamples: Its sandboxes for lazy with Suspense and the top-level declaration fix are as reusable as our examples.
followUpConfusion: It answers the core traps authoritatively: default export only, cached promise, rejection to the nearest error boundary, and state reset when lazy is declared inside a component.

actionableExamples: Add a measured before-and-after bundle size for the route split, so the payoff is shown with numbers.
followUpConfusion: Add the state reset symptom (inputs clearing on every parent render) next to the top-level declaration comment, so readers can recognize the bug.

competitors.label: Module Federation
competitors.selectionReason: The webpack concept page is the canonical source for module federation containers, remotes and shared modules.
theirStrengths: Precise definitions of containers, remotes and shared modules, dynamic remotes, and the eager consumption error with the async boundary fix.
theirGaps: Build-architecture use cases only: no team trade-offs, no React-specific traps and no comparison with code splitting.

realWorldUseCases: A broken or slow remote now breaks a region of the host in production
Its use cases are build-architecture ones (separate builds per page, a components library as a container), not the team and failure trade-offs an interviewer probes.
actionableExamples: Its configuration examples and the async boundary diff are as concrete as ours.
followUpConfusion: It documents the eager consumption error, dynamic remotes and share scopes in more technical depth; our React-specific traps (singleton React, Invalid hook call) do not outweigh that.

actionableExamples: Add a dynamic remote example, with the remote URL resolved at runtime, for apps whose remote locations differ per environment.
followUpConfusion: Add the follow-up on versioning remotes: how a host pins or rolls back a remote when a release breaks it.
